transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. Um, I guess the main thing is I get pulled off track really easily. Like I’ll be working on a dashboard I’m supposed to finish, and then one Slack ping comes in, or even a song lyric gets stuck in my head, or I suddenly think of another project idea, and then I’ve completely lost what I was doing.

It’s frustrating because it feels like I was right there, and then the thread is just gone.
Does this getting pulled off track happen in other parts of your life too, like at home or in conversations, or mainly just at work?

Yeah, mostly that same kind of thing. Like, I notice it when I’m trying to finish something and then anything pulls me away—a ping, or a random thought, or I’ll get a lyric stuck in my head and suddenly I’m not even on the thing anymore. The dashboard was just the easiest example because it’s been happening there a lot.

I mean, I guess it’s not only the dashboard, it’s more like I lose the thread really fast once something interrupts me. Then I’m sitting there trying to remember, “Wait, what was I doing?”
Thinking back to when you were a child, were you already someone who got distracted easily?

Yeah, I think so. I mean, I didn’t think of it that way at the time, obviously, but my elementary school teachers would write stuff on report cards like that I rushed through worksheets or didn’t follow all the directions because I’d lose track of what I was supposed to do.

And group work was… yeah, I’d talk over people sometimes. Not trying to be rude, I just would get excited and jump in. My parents also used to have to sit next to me during homework, because if they didn’t I’d kind of wander off or start doing something else before I finished. I remember sharpening pencils a lot for no real reason, like suddenly that was the most important thing.
Have there been times when you felt unusually energized or high, and that was when your mind was especially hard to keep on track?

Um… I’m not sure. I don’t know if I’d say “high” exactly. Like, sometimes I get really into something and I’m more keyed up, but I also get distracted when I’m just normal or tired or whatever.

Sorry, I’m thinking of like finals week, because everyone is kind of wired then, and my roommate had this whole color-coded calendar thing that made me feel like I should be doing that too, but—yeah, I don’t know that it’s tied to feeling unusually energized. I haven’t really noticed a pattern like that.
Do you get unwanted thoughts that keep coming back even when you try to ignore them?

Um… unwanted thoughts like, over and over? I’m not totally sure. I mean, I definitely get random thoughts stuck in my head sometimes, like something I forgot to do or a song or replaying a conversation, but I don’t know if that’s what you mean.

Like sometimes I’ll be trying to read and then suddenly I’m thinking about whether I answered a text from two days ago, and then that reminds me of—sorry, that’s probably not what you asked. I guess I haven’t really noticed thoughts that feel intrusive in that way, like I’m trying really hard to ignore them and they keep forcing their way back. At least not that I can think of right now.
Do you often find yourself worrying a lot, even when there isn’t an obvious reason to?

I mean… I worry sometimes, yeah, but I don’t know if it’s “a lot” or for no reason. Usually there’s some reason, like school stuff or forgetting something, or… actually I was just thinking about this thing where I’ll check my backpack because I’m convinced I left my charger, but that’s probably more practical than worry.

So, um, I guess I wouldn’t say I’m constantly worrying out of nowhere. At least I haven’t noticed that being a big thing.
Do you often have trouble staying focused on a task even when there isn’t anything around to interrupt you?

Yeah, definitely. Like, even if it’s totally quiet and my phone isn’t right there, I can sit down to read a research article for class or watch some UX tutorial, and after a few minutes I’ll realize my eyes have just been moving across the page or the video is still playing, but I have no idea what I just took in.

It’s weird because nothing even has to interrupt me. I’ll think I’m paying attention, and then I’m like, wait, what was that whole last section about? Then I have to go back, which is annoying, especially with articles that are already kind of dense.
Has this distractibility caused problems for you in more than one part of your life, like school, work, or relationships?

Yeah… I think it has. Mostly with school-type and creative/work stuff, I guess. Like I’m not officially working, but I’ve done small freelance design things, and I’ve lost a couple of those because I didn’t follow through cleanly or people couldn’t count on me to get things done the way I said I would.

And there was this portfolio competition I really wanted to submit to—actually I spent forever picking which pieces to include, which is kind of funny because that wasn’t even the hard part—but I ended up missing out because I couldn’t stay on track with all the steps. That felt really bad.

Also with friends or people I collaborate with, they’ll still say they like my ideas, but I can tell some of them are hesitant to work with me because they’re not sure I’ll be reliable. So… yeah, more than one area, I’d say.
Do you often feel physically restless, like you need to move or fidget even when you’re supposed to stay seated?

Yeah, I do. Like if I’m in a long Zoom call or I’m supposed to just sit and work quietly in one spot, I start getting this kind of uncomfortable pressure in my body, like I need to get up or pace around.

Sometimes I’ll just start messing with something in my hands, like a pen or whatever’s nearby. It’s not always super dramatic, but sitting still for too long feels… weirdly hard.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you felt down or lost interest in things most of the day nearly every day?

Um… I don’t know. I mean, I’ve had bad stretches where I’m unmotivated or kind of blah, especially when I’m behind on stuff, but I’m not sure if it was like most of the day every day for two weeks.

It’s hard for me to track time like that, honestly. Like I’ll think something was “all month” and then realize it was three days, or the opposite. So… I don’t think I can say yes for sure.
Do you often have trouble organizing tasks or keeping track of the steps you need to finish something?

Yeah, definitely. Like if someone gives me a list of revisions, I’ll do the first couple right away, and I’ll feel like, okay, I’m on it. But then I’ll kind of drift into redesigning some totally different part because I suddenly think it would look better, and then I’ll forget there was one small change they specifically asked for.

And it’s always something stupid but important, like changing a label or fixing the spacing on one thing, and then that’s the thing I leave unfinished. I don’t mean to, I just sort of lose the thread of the steps.
Do you often interrupt people or blurt things out before they finish talking?

Yeah… I think so. Not always like cutting people off mid-sentence on purpose, but in brainstorms especially, if I suddenly get an idea I’ll just say it right away before they’re done explaining.

Or if we’re in Figma, I might start adding something to the board while someone is still talking through what they meant, because in my head I’m like, “Oh, I see where this could go.” And then afterward I realize I probably came off kind of pushy or like I wasn’t listening, even though I was just excited and didn’t want to lose the idea.
Do you often act on impulse, like doing things before thinking them through?

Yeah, kind of. Like in brainstorming, I’ll get this idea and I’ll just say it before the person has even finished explaining what they meant.

Or if we’re in Figma, I might literally start moving things around or adding something to their board while they’re still talking, because I’m like, “Oh wait, I know what would help.” And then afterward I’m like… okay, that probably seemed pushy. I don’t mean it that way, I’m just excited and I guess I act before I really think about how it’s coming across.
Have you ever had a time when you felt unusually euphoric or unusually irritable for several days in a row?

Um… I don’t think so? Like, I definitely have days where I’m really excited about something or I get annoyed, but I don’t know if I’d call it unusually euphoric for several days.

I’m trying to think… sometimes if I’m working on a project I like, I’ll be in a really good mood and kind of obsess over it, but that’s more just because I’m into it. And irritability, maybe here and there, but not like a whole stretch where it felt really abnormal. I guess I’m not totally sure what counts as “unusually” in that sense.
Do you often forget everyday things, like appointments, deadlines, or where you put important items?

Yeah, pretty often. Like I’ll forget really basic things unless I set reminders—returning a client call, sending a follow-up email, stuff like that.

And even with reminders, sometimes I’ll swipe them away because I’m in the middle of something, and then it’s just… gone from my brain. Or I’ll be going to a meetup and somehow forget my sketchbook, which is ridiculous because that’s kind of the whole point. I’ll remember like snacks or my water bottle, but not the actual thing I needed.
